renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  id: mapped_reads_bar
  title: Mapped reads before and after the mapping-quality filter
  description: |-
    Each bar is the number of mapped reads of a sample at one stage, before or after the mapping-quality filter. It answers how many reads survive the filter and whether samples differ in depth.
    How to read: a post-filter bar close to the pre-filter one means the filter removed little. A large drop points to many low-quality or multi-mapping reads, so check the reference, the trimming and the library. Very uneven bars across samples call for normalisation downstream.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-flagstat.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: mapped_reads
    color: stage
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      mapped_reads: Mapped reads
      stage: Filter stage

- component: card
  id: mapped_reads_total
  title: Mapped reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of mapped reads over the samples and stages in view, with the smallest and largest beside it. It answers how deep the alignments are and how uneven.
    How to read: a large gap between the smallest and the largest count means uneven depth. Filter to one stage to compare samples on equal footing.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-flagstat.html
  column: mapped_reads
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median, with the smallest and largest

- component: card
  id: mapped_pct_card
  title: Mapping rate before filtering
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of reads that map, before the mapping-quality filter, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how well the reads align to the reference.
    How to read: a high median means most reads belong to the reference. A low value or a long box points to contamination, the wrong reference or adapters left in the reads. Open the bar chart to find the samples responsible.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-flagstat.html
  column: mapped_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('stage') == 'pre-filter'
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Flagstat counts
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample at one filter stage with its read counts and percentages. It answers the exact numbers behind the chart and cards.
    How to read: sort by mapped percentage to find the weakest alignments.

- component: card
  id: reads_by_contig_class
  title: Mapped reads by contig class
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of mapped reads, the second number is the largest count on a single contig, and the bar splits the reads into autosome, X, Y, mitochondrion and other contigs. It answers where the reads went.
    How to read: most reads should fall on autosomes. A large share on other contigs points to alt, unplaced or decoy sequence soaking up reads, and a large mitochondrial share points to a stressed or poorly prepared library.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-idxstats.html
  column: mapped_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: contig_class
  caption: reads, by contig class

- component: card
  id: mito_share
  title: Mitochondrial share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of mapped reads on the mitochondrial genome, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how much of each library is mitochondrial.
    How to read: a sample far above its peers wasted sequencing on the mitochondrion, often from lysis or a protocol that does not deplete it. Acceptable levels depend on the assay, so compare against samples of the same type.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-idxstats.html
  column: mapped_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('contig_class') == 'mitochondrion'
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: figure
  id: contig_class_bars
  title: Mapped reads by contig class per sample
  description: |-
    Each segment is the share of a sample's mapped reads that fall on one class of contig. It answers how the composition of mapped reads differs between samples.
    How to read: samples should look alike. A sample with a taller mitochondrial or other segment, or an odd Y share, stands out from its peers and may be a swap or a quality problem. Open the table for the contigs behind a segment.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-idxstats.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: mapped_pct
    color: contig_class
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      mapped_pct: Share of mapped reads (%)
      contig_class: Contig class

- component: table
  title: Reads per contig
  description: |-
    Each row is a contig of a sample with its length, its class, its mapped reads and its share of the sample. It answers the exact count on every contig.
    How to read: sort by reads per megabase to find contigs that attract more reads than their length explains.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: read_length_profile
  title: Read length distribution
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the number of reads at every read length in the alignment. It answers how long the aligned reads are and whether the length is uniform.
    How to read: short-read data draws one sharp peak at the sequenced length, and trimmed reads draw a spread below it. A long flat tail is expected for long-read data. Samples with a different shape were trimmed or sequenced differently.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-stats.html
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Read length (bp)
    y_title: Reads
  roles:
    series: series
    x: bin
    y: n_reads

- component: advanced_viz
  id: coverage_distribution
  title: Coverage depth distribution
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the number of bases covered at every depth. It answers how evenly the reads cover the reference.
    How to read: a narrow hump means even coverage and a long right tail means a few regions are over-covered. A tall bar at depth zero or one means much of the target is barely sequenced, so raise depth or check the library.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-stats.html
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Coverage depth
    y_title: Bases
  roles:
    series: series
    x: bin
    y: n_bases

- component: advanced_viz
  id: indel_spectrum
  title: Indel length spectrum
  description: |-
    Each line is the number of insertions or deletions of one length in a sample, drawn separately for each direction. It answers whether insertions and deletions are balanced.
    How to read: counts fall quickly with length. Deletions far outnumbering insertions, or the reverse, can point to a systematic error of the sequencing platform, which long-read data often shows.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-stats.html
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Indel length (bp)
    y_title: Indels
  roles:
    series: series
    x: bin
    y: n_indels

- component: card
  title: Reads mapped
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of reads that are mapped, and the box shows the spread across samples. It answers how well the reads align.
    How to read: a high median is expected. A low value or a long box means some samples align poorly, from contamination or the wrong reference.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-stats.html
  column: reads_mapped_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Alignment identity
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of aligned bases that match the reference (one minus the mismatch error rate), and the box shows the spread. It answers how closely the reads agree with the reference.
    How to read: higher means closer agreement. Long-read data sits lower than short reads, so compare samples from the same platform.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-stats.html
  column: identity_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Average read length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of each sample's average read length, and the box shows the spread. It answers how long the reads are.
    How to read: samples of one run should agree. A sample far from its peers was trimmed or sequenced differently.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-stats.html
  column: average_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Longest read
  description: |-
    The hero number is the longest read seen in any sample, and the second number is the median of the per-sample maximums. It answers how far the read length tail extends.
    How to read: a single very long read can be a chimera or an artefact, so the median of the maximums is the steadier value.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-stats.html
  column: maximum_length
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: longest read, with the median of the maximums

- component: card
  title: Supplementary alignments
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of supplementary alignments, which are the extra pieces of reads that align in several places, and the second number is the largest count in one sample. It answers how fragmented the alignments are.
    How to read: a high count is common in long-read data and can mark structural variants or chimeric reads. A sample far above the rest deserves a look.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-stats.html
  column: supplementary_alignments
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: alignments, with the largest sample

- component: card
  title: Average base quality
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of each sample's average base quality, and the box shows the spread. It answers how reliable the base calls are.
    How to read: higher is better, and the scale depends on the sequencing platform. A sample well below its peers may have a failed run.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-stats.html
  column: average_quality
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Mapped reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of mapped reads and the second number is the median per sample. It answers how much aligned data the run holds.
    How to read: a median far below the total divided by the sample count means a few samples hold most of the data. Open the table for the counts.
    Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-stats.html
  column: reads_mapped
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: reads, with the median per sample

- component: table
  title: Alignment statistics
  description: |-
    Each row is a histogram bin or a summary line of a sample. It answers the exact values behind the profiles and cards.
    How to read: filter the section column to read one distribution, or to the summary rows for per-sample totals.
  page_size: 25
